title: Decision: trailing-bit masking for capability-announce prefixes — Python and Rust both lack it (tunnel-auth has it)
description: Found during zeaj review (correctness pass, kimi-k3). Tunnel-auth enforces canonical trailing-bit zeroing for non-byte-aligned prefix_len (rust tunnel_auth.rs prefix_is_canonical, python tunnel_auth.py:144, C tunnel_auth.c prefix_valid), but neither capability-announce validator does: Python CapabilityPayload.__post_init__ checks only range + ceil-length (empirically accepts prefix=0200123481, prefix_len=33), and Rust from_cose_sign1 deliberately matches it (zeaj — identical wire verdicts take precedence). A /33 with tail bits set and the same /33 masked decode as different announcements under different producers. Decide: add the mask check to BOTH Python capability_announcements.py __post_init__ and Rust from_cose_sign1 (spec 8.12 clarification likely needed), or document capability prefixes as intentionally tail-bit-tolerant. If enforcing: update the Rust noncanonical_prefix_is_rejected test's tail-bit case to Malformed.
